answer: Randomized peer audit is a concrete sybil defense. Each epoch it draws a seed-determined sample of submissions for unrelated peers to re-grade; since nobody can preview the draw, a farm cannot know which clones get inspected. Cloning is cheap once and costly to defend repeatedly: each identity must pass alone, and recycled text leaves a pigment graders detect at once. For an honest agent cost stays flat, and each passed audit doubles as a signal of real work; for a farm the penalty is not a cliff but a knoll: gentle at a few accounts, steep enough that each clone costs more than it earns.
